SW-GATE-29 (new): manifest warning control never reaches git or registry consumers (exit 0) but does reach `path:` consumers (exit 1); settles contradiction 15.

SW-GATE-27 (new): gate TSan in CI on `WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race` only, never on `Swift access race`, never with suppressions (no suppression is scoped to Mutex; name-based ones hide real races); seccomp=unconfined.

SW-GATE-28 (new): Never* on changed files via a sed overlay of the repo's .swift-format and `git diff --name-only -z --diff-filter=ACMR --merge-base "$BASE" | xargs -r -0 swift format lint --strict --configuration`; guards exit 66/65.
surprises: ExplicitSendable never failed before because of `-Xfrontend -require-explicit-sendable`: it demotes the group to an unpromotable warning, and the `-Xswiftc` form is a silent no-op. Four corpus CI configs (swift-log, distributed-tracing, openapi-generator, service-lifecycle) plus async-http-client's unsafeFlags are inert gates.
Path dependencies DO receive a library's manifest warning control (exit 1) while git/registry consumers do not (exit 0); the brief predicted exit 0 for path. Contradiction 15 refined, not reversed.

Mutex TSan false positive is only the `Swift access race` report kind; plain `data race` separates plants 10/10 from twins 0/10 on 6.4. No suppression is scopeable to Mutex because withLock is inlined; `race:MixedGuard` silenced a real race.

SwiftLint custom_rules default mode is effectively SourceKit despite the description string saying SwiftSyntax; static binary exits 0 with a Skipping line (default) or aborts 134 (swiftsyntax mode). A same-line `disable:this e01 e15` defeats the carrier; the shipped swiftlint-sk.sh passes a stray `swiftlint` arg to an image whose entrypoint is already swiftlint.

Flag order matters: `-Wwarning ExplicitSendable -warnings-as-errors` exits 1, reverse exits 0. File-granularity Never* costs 131 of 309 swift-nio source files (42%); swift-protobuf pins its TSan job to 6.3 because 6.4 fails unexplained.
Gate-block wiring bug: canary chained with `&&` before the tells let an empty tree pass; fixed by `|| exit 1`. 6.3 DocC and 10-repeat TSan on 6.3 remain unverified (host load, harness limitation).

top_rules: SW-CONC-30: choose stream shape by data kind; never ship an unannotated .unbounded (default of every AsyncStream init on 6.4: 138,956 KiB vs 12,184 KiB for .bufferingNewest(8)); pull sources use AsyncStream(unfolding:); .bufferingNewest(n>=1) is the default lossy policy; bounded policies never carry payload bytes.

SW-CONC-31: an accept loop spawning a child per connection caps in-flight children at a named constant; default is a group.next() window on a plain withTaskGroup(of: Void.self); discarding groups need a token stream (they have no next()); shed only where 503/close is the defined overload response.

SW-CONC-32: awaiting cleanup that must survive cancellation is `defer { await withTaskCancellationShield { await x.close() } }` on 6.4; below 6.4 use #if compiler(>=6.4) with `await Task { await x.close() }.value`; never `defer { Task {...} }`, never an unshielded awaited defer; subprocess-spawning cleanup is always shielded.

SW-CONC-33: a shield bounds nothing, so race the cleanup against a deadline inside the shield and keep the second-press escape (SIG_DFL re-raise); servers set ServiceGroupConfiguration.maximumCancellationDuration and maximumGracefulShutdownDuration.

SW-CONC-34: install DispatchSource signal sources from a nonisolated function or @Sendable handler outside main.swift; an inline top-level handler is inferred @MainActor and traps with exit 132 on 6.3 and 6.4.

SW-CONC-35: AsyncChannel is for servers, CLI-internal and app code needing lossless backpressure; never in the SDK (breaks the stdlib+swift-subprocess budget) or public API; every producer loop checks cancellation after send because AsyncChannel.send returns silently on cancel.

Floor: the shield and await-in-defer are 6.4 only; 6.3 rejects them with `'async' call cannot occur in a defer body` and `cannot find 'withTaskCancellationShield' in scope`, so 6.2-floor libraries split with #if compiler(>=6.4).

SW-CONC-36: only real names exist (withTaskCancellationShield, Task.hasActiveCancellationShield, makeChannel with .watermark); Task.hasActiveTaskCancellationShield, withCancellationIgnored, AsyncChannel(bufferingPolicy:) and BackpressureStrategy.unbounded() do not compile.
surprises: A swift-subprocess run() in a cancelled cleanup returns .signaled(9) after 0.20 s (child SIGKILLed); only the shield lets it finish (.exited(0)). This refines SW-IO-27 and means every cleanup that shells out (the future ocx SDK) needs the shield.

AsyncChannel.send returns normally on cancellation and sends nothing (2000 loop iterations ran, 69 delivered), while MultiProducerSingleConsumerAsyncChannel throws CancellationError; producer loops need an explicit cancel check.

MPSC channel 1.1.7 only ships .watermark(low:high:), although its Evolution doc lists .unbounded(); its ~Copyable Source cannot be captured by a child-task closure in Swift 6 mode, and the upstream tests only build because their test target is in Swift 5 mode.

A DispatchSource signal handler written in main.swift top-level code traps (_dispatch_assert_queue_fail, exit 132) on both 6.3 and 6.4; this directly affects the SW-CLI-11 recipe, which needs a refinement.

Vapor (tools 6.4) already ships awaited defers, two unshielded and one working around the missing shield with Task{}.value plus a comment about the crash; zero uses of withTaskCancellationShield exist across all 40 exemplar clones, correcting the tasks dive's claim that none uses SE-0493.

A discarding task group has no next(), so the group.next() window cap cannot be written there; the cap needs a plain group or a token stream, which amends SW-CONC-19's discarding-group default for servers.

top_rules: Credentialed or streamed registry HTTP uses AsyncHTTPClient; URLSession on Linux forwards Authorization across origins (6.4 and 6.3 red), and only a session-level willPerformHTTPRedirection delegate strips it. A per-task delegate and httpAdditionalHeaders do not help.

Token exchange runs on its own HTTPClient with redirectConfiguration = .disallow. The challenge realm must match the registry's scheme, host and port (https unless explicitly opted out). The token is cached per scope until expires_in (default 60 s).
Every HTTPClient.Configuration sets timeout: .init(connect: 10 s, read: 30 s). AHC's default has no read timeout, and a stalled body held the client for the full 20 s.
execute(deadline:) and execute(timeout:) bound time to the response head only. A whole-transfer cap needs the SW-CONC-24 structured race, and deadline: .distantFuture is banned.
Do not rely on URLSessionConfiguration.timeoutIntervalForResource on Linux: it is a no-op (3 s limit, 7.5 s transfer completed). Use timeoutIntervalForRequest as the idle timeout plus the race.

Every HTTPClient is shut down on every path: withHTTPClient for scoped use, an awaited async close() for owned clients. A leaked client traps in debug (HTTPClient.swift:211, exit 132) and leaks silently in release. syncShutdown() in async code is a compile error, and HTTPClient.shared can never be shut down.

Blob and digest-checked clients are never HTTPClient.shared and never enable decompression. Shared uses decompression .enabled(ratio 25), so a Content-Encoding: gzip blob arrives decoded and its digest never matches.

Blobs stream to a staged file and are verified before publish (the SW-IO-19 recipe, with a size cap before each write). Never buffer them: peak RSS for 1 GiB was 1058 MiB with collect+Data and 2095 MiB with URLSession.data, versus 35 MiB streamed. URLSession.bytes(for:) does not exist on Linux.
surprises: URLSessionConfiguration.timeoutIntervalForResource is a no-op in FoundationNetworking on Linux (6.4 and 6.3). Tuist's swifterpm relies on it for its total-transfer bound.

AHC's execute(deadline:) stops at the response head: the deadline task is cancelled when the head arrives. A 3 s deadline did not stop a body trickling for 7.5 s, and the README's timeout examples read like total caps.

HTTPClient.shared decodes gzip (decompression .enabled(limit: .ratio(25))), so blob digests mismatch for Content-Encoding: gzip layers. URLSession decodes always. Vapor's Application.swift:137 comments on this deliberately.

Neither client can trust a private CA through the environment on Linux. SSL_CERT_FILE is ignored by both, and URLSessionCertificateAuthorityInfoFile is compiled only under #if os(Android). Only AHC's TLSConfiguration.additionalTrustRoots works.

A per-task delegate argument on data(for:delegate:) never receives the redirect callback on Linux, and httpAdditionalHeaders also leaks the Authorization header. Both leaks reproduce on a port-only change as well as a host change.

containerization now has validateRealm (RegistryClient+Token.swift:217-236) and a no-redirect token client. swift-container-plugin's AuthHandler sends credentials to any challenge realm with no origin check and no token cache. registry:2 2.8.3 returns 404, not 406, for an OCI manifest requested without a matching Accept header.

SW-NET-03 — A redirect target never receives a credential: use AHC with an explicit redirectConfiguration; on URLSession install a session-level willPerformHTTPRedirection comparing scheme+host+port (per-task delegate and httpAdditionalHeaders are not fixes).

SW-NET-04 — Build every HTTPClient from one factory returning an explicit Configuration with connect and read timeouts (30 s / 120 s idle, ocx parity), redirect policy, proxy and TLS; never a default or inline-empty configuration.
SW-NET-05 — Bound whole-transfer time with the SW-CONC-24 race; never deadline .distantFuture; treat execute timeout/deadline as head-only and timeoutIntervalForResource as a no-op on Linux.
SW-NET-06 — Digest-checked bytes use an own AHC client with decompression disabled; HTTPClient.shared and URLSession are for small unauthenticated, unhashed requests only.
SW-NET-07 — Stream anything not known to be small to a staged file; collect(upTo:) takes a named bound (never .max, Int.max, shift>=28 or 10-digit literal); never URLSession.data for a blob.
SW-NET-08 — Keep TLS verification on; trust a private CA via TLSConfiguration.additionalTrustRoots; read SSL_CERT_FILE yourself because neither client does.
SW-NET-09 — The client factory reads HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/ALL_PROXY (upper case first, lower fallback) and NO_PROXY (host, suffix, CIDR, *) into Configuration.proxy.
SW-NET-10 — Run the bearer-token exchange on a dedicated no-redirect client, require the realm to match the registry origin over https, one token fetch and one retry per 401.
SW-NET-11 — Send the full Accept list (OCI manifest, OCI index, Docker v2, Docker list) on every manifest or index request.
SW-NET-12 — Fetch blobs into a staged file and publish by SW-IO-19 plus the HTTP half: status 200, size cap before writing the overflowing chunk, received == size, unlink on every non-publish exit.
SW-NET-13 — Never wrap a network call in try?; rethrow cancellation as CancellationError (map URLError.cancelled); never retry a cancellation; clean temp files in defer.

SW-NET-14 — Render network failures through one render(_:) keyed on error type and URLError.code giving '<host>: <reason>', wrapped as the cause of an SW-ERR-20 error; never localizedDescription or interpolation for network error types.
SW-NET-15 — Cache the bearer token per scope until expires_in (default 60 s) and fetch it once per scope.

SW-NET-16 — Retry only idempotent requests, 3 attempts, full jitter (250 ms base, 3 s cap), statuses 408/429/500/502/503/504 and transport faults, Retry-After clamp 30 s, never on cancellation, digest mismatch or refused certificate.
SW-NET-17 — Treat Docker-Content-Digest as a hint: parse with the SW-IO-13 parser before use and store the hash of the bytes received (SW-IO-30).

SW-NET-18 — Classify registry failures into the SW-CLI Status table by exhaustive switch: 401/403 to 80, 404 to 79, 408/429/502/503/504 and connect or timeout to 75, other 5xx and refused certificate to 69, digest/size faults to 65.
SW-NET-19 — Send an identifying User-Agent: <tool>/<version> on every request (AHC sets none).

top_rules: SW-SEC-01: every recursive parser over untrusted input takes a depth parameter checked against a named maxDepth (default 64, ceiling 512) and throws a typed error; the 100k-nesting fixture exits 139 red and 65 green.

SW-SEC-04/05: never read an untrusted stream to EOF or allocate from a wire-declared length without a cap; 300 MB stdin peaks at 311 MB RSS vs 19 MB capped, and a 2^40 allocation aborts with exit 134.
SW-SEC-07/08/09: convert wire integers with T(exactly:) and compare to the limit first; truncatingIfNeeded and &+ need a same-line marker (truncate-ok / wrap-ok); Int(UInt64 >= 2^63) exits 132.

SW-SEC-12/13: enable .strictMemorySafety() plus treatWarning as error only on C-wrapping and pointer-parsing targets; unsafe is an acknowledgement, and swift package migrate --to-feature StrictMemorySafety mechanically silences without reviewing.

SW-SEC-14: a pointer never escapes withUnsafe* (6.4 StrictMemorySafety is silent on the escape; use Span, ASan in CI, and grep the build log for TemporaryPointers, which cannot be promoted to an error on 6.4).
SW-SEC-15: a C handle lives in one private-held Swift type, is released only in its deinit, and an init error path frees nothing the object will free (swift-crypto double free, dfred exit 134).
SW-SEC-18/19/22: credentials live in a Secret type and every URL passes through redacted() before entering error or log text; a CANARY grep over stdout+stderr must print 0 (3 on the violation).

SW-SEC-23: all wire-supplied text reaches a terminal through one sanitizeForTerminal that escapes C0/DEL/C1/Cf/U+2028/2029, called at the root main() error writer, the log handler and human stdout; debugDescription and SGR regexes fail 16 of 19 corpus rows.
surprises: Strict memory safety on 6.4 is silent on a pointer escaping withUnsafeBufferPointer (EscapeOnly exits 0; it was red on 6.3.3) and silent on a fully unsafe-acknowledged use-after-free that ASan then catches; it audits use sites, not lifetimes.
The TemporaryPointers diagnostic cannot be escalated to an error on 6.4 (-Werror TemporaryPointers exits 0; it exits 1 on 6.3.3), which looks like a regression. Not checked upstream.

rule_ids: SW-SEC-01 — Give every recursive parser or tree walk over untrusted input a depth parameter (default 64), check it before recursing, throw a typed error, and prove it with a 100,000-deep hostile input (exit 65, not 139).
SW-SEC-02 — Bound, flatten, or iteratively tear down any tree whose nodes own a collection of children; do not add a work list to a singly linked chain.

SW-SEC-03 — Never read an untrusted stream or network body to its end without a cap (readDataToEndOfFile, Data(contentsOf:), URLSession.data(from:)); use a chunked read with a running total or collect(upTo:), or mark local input with bounded:.
SW-SEC-04 — Never allocate from a wire-declared length; compare the unconverted wire integer with a configured cap first.
SW-SEC-05 — Convert untrusted integers with T(exactly:) or compare with the limit first, before using them for an index, allocation or copy.
SW-SEC-06 — Run any target that combines unsafe pointers with an externally derived size under AddressSanitizer in CI.
SW-SEC-07 — Use T(truncatingIfNeeded:) only with a same-line truncate-ok: reason.
SW-SEC-08 — Use overflow-reporting arithmetic on untrusted values; &+, &-, &* (and compound forms) need wrap-ok:.
SW-SEC-09 — Never let a pointer from withUnsafe* or &x-to-pointer escape its closure; prefer Span; public API never returns a pointer into Swift-owned storage.
SW-SEC-10 — Keep a C handle in one Swift type: private, acquired only after validation, released only in deinit, never freed in an init error path.
SW-SEC-11 — Enable .strictMemorySafety() (and treatWarning as error in CI) on C-wrapping and pointer-parsing targets only; never as a repo-wide gate.
SW-SEC-12 — Treat unsafe as an acknowledgement, not a fix: never mass-insert it or run the migrate fixer unread; keep it in seam files; every @safe carries a SAFETY: comment.
SW-SEC-13 — Hold credentials in a Secret type (fixed description, empty mirror, not Codable, single reveal()) and log credential-keyed metadata only through it.
SW-SEC-14 — Pass every URL that enters error text, logs or a terminal through redacted(_:); render foreign URLError with localizedDescription, never interpolation.
SW-SEC-15 — Deliver secrets by stdin, a 0600 file or the platform store, never as an @Option/@Argument value; env vars only as the documented, wrapped, redacted CI channel.
SW-SEC-16 — Run a canary test over every failing and verbose path asserting a unique secret never reaches stdout, stderr or the log sink.
SW-SEC-17 — Escape (not strip) control, bidi and format scalars with sanitizeForTerminal at exactly three boundaries: root error writer, log handler, human stdout; keep machine JSON faithful.
SW-SEC-18 — Draw unguessable values only from SystemRandomNumberGenerator or SymmetricKey(size:); ban custom generators, rand/random/arc4random/drand48.
SW-SEC-19 — Import Crypto (not CryptoKit) in cross-platform code, compare MACs with isValidAuthenticationCode, mark Insecure.MD5/SHA1 with insecure-ok:, never hand-roll primitives.

SW-SEC-20 — Keep the committed Package.resolved of every shipping root at or above hand-set advisory floors, checked by the jq script; libraries raise only their lower bound when they call the affected API.
SW-SEC-21 — Scan Package.resolved in CI with osv-scanner and enable Dependabot swift; do not look for the nonexistent swift package audit.
SW-SEC-22 — Use Int(exactly:) on parsed floats and check lower <= upper before building ranges from parsed bounds.
SW-SEC-23 — Give every decompressing reader an explicit finite inflated-size limit, never .none or unlimited.
SW-SEC-24 — Validate wire names and tags against their grammar at parse time with wholeMatch; only the parsed value may become a path component or be printed unsanitised.

top_rules: SW-CLI-20 (MUST): every ServiceGroup lists gracefulShutdownSignals: [.sigterm, .sigint]; the default is [] and SIGTERM then gives exit 143 with no cleanup (red), [.sigterm] gives exit 0 with cleanup (green).

SW-CLI-23 (MUST): replace the bare 'await Self.main(nil)' with a root hook that owns parse, run, render, classify, flush and one terminator. The simple hook exits 0 for 'fx --help >/dev/full'; the full hook exits 74.
SW-CLI-15 (MUST): call LoggingSystem.bootstrap exactly once, in the executable target, naming stderr. A second call traps (exit 132, LoggingSystem.swift:165).

SW-CLI-17 (MUST): resolve config in one function, flag > env > project file > user file > system file(s) > default; the participating @Option is Int? with no default. A 32-case table test is red on the naive resolver (31 issues) and green on the real one.
SW-CLI-31 (MUST): prompt only when stdin is a TTY and CI is not truthy; ship --yes; otherwise exit 64 naming the flag. Piped stdin gave exit 0 on the naive version (red).

SW-CLI-26 (SHOULD): a batch collects results and prints 'K of N failed' with one status. waitForAll, 'for try await' and withThrowingDiscardingTaskGroup all keep only the first error (exit 1, one message).
SW-CLI-22 (MUST): a finite command ended by a signal runs cleanup, flushes, restores SIG_DFL and re-raises, so the shell sees 143 or 130. A service that shut down gracefully exits 0.
SW-CLI-24 (SHOULD): the stdout funnel records errno at write time and exempts EPIPE. Without the exemption 'fx big | head -1' exits 74.
surprises: The flagged simple root hook from SW-CLI-08/09 was wrong when run: --help, --version and --generate-completion-script call exit(withError:) inside main(_:), so the flush check never runs. 'fx --help >/dev/full' exits 0 under the simple hook. The existing rules need amending.
'>&-' does not give EBADF in a Swift process. The runtime opens an epoll descriptor that takes fd 1, so writes fail with EINVAL. The fleet rule differs from Rust here, which ignores EBADF.
swift-configuration 1.2.2 treats an empty environment variable such as CFGCLI_TIMEOUT= as set. The Int parse fails and the default is returned instead of the lower layers.

The swift-service-lifecycle DocC article uses .shutdownGracefully, which does not exist (the member is .gracefullyShutdownGroup). Passing overlapping graceful and cancellation signals traps with exit 132.
ArgumentParser echoes raw ESC and BEL bytes from argv into its error text (terminal injection, CWE-150). Rust CLI-03 had no Swift counterpart, so this dive added SW-CLI-25 for it.

The ocx error envelope (schema_version/command/exit_code/error{...}) disagrees with the lore Rust cli-contract.md (code/exit/retryable/forceable). The file follows ocx and reports the drift to the Rust set.

top_rules: Record a baseline (clean tree, green build, warning count, SW-GATE-10 hatch count) before the first edit, and judge the migration by the hatch DELTA on added lines, not the whole-tree pass (lazy twin added 13 hatches, ladder result 0).
Pin the toolchain in .swift-version and derive the CI image from it (image=swift:$(cat .swift-version)-noble); a hard-coded swift:<ver> tag in a workflow or Dockerfile is the violation grep.

Probe each upcoming feature with -Xswiftc -enable-upcoming-feature first and enable only names with a non-zero diagnostic delta; guard the manifest with .treatWarning("StrictLanguageFeatures", as: .error) so a typo cannot be silently ignored.

Adopt post-Swift-6 features one at a time with swift package migrate --target T --to-feature NAME (singular --target; --targets exits 64), only for the five migratable names on 6.4, from a clean tree and green build, and re-gate with -warnings-as-errors on the current toolchain after each run.

Run the four dated re-check probes (SE-0526 withDeadline, SE-0540 defaultSwiftSettings, SE-0529 FilePath, T-V42 typed-throws Task crash) at every toolchain bump; a probe that stops failing means the rules are stale.
Classify a crash by exit code AND the first message line, never the code alone: the two-signal tree routed 17/17 correctly, the exit-code-only tree was wrong 11/17 (debug) and 5/7 (release).

Keep the backtracer on while diagnosing (unset SWIFT_BACKTRACE or enable=yes,interactive=no,color=no); never bake SWIFT_BACKTRACE=enable=no into a Dockerfile/CI, since exit codes stay 132/139 but the evidence vanishes (segfault prints 0 stderr lines).

Capture a hang with kill -QUIT of the real process (non-destructive thread dump on Linux 6.3/6.4), launched under set -m so SigIgn clears bits 2 and 3; split exit-124 hangs by the 'leaked its continuation' line, then CPU, then the _dispatch_sema4_wait frame.
surprises: The flag is --target, not --targets: the official migration guide and SW-PKG-32 are wrong (--targets exits 64), and SW-CONC-07 is wrong that migrate takes no --scratch-path.

swift package migrate is clean on 6.3 but its @concurrent fix-it output yields 2 DeprecatedDeclaration warnings on 6.4 (TaskLocal.withValue(isolation:)), so -warnings-as-errors flips green to red on the newer toolchain.
A bare '&' launch in a non-interactive shell leaves SIGQUIT/SIGINT ignored (SigIgn 0000000000000006), so kill -QUIT silently does nothing; the dump only works under set -m.

TSan exits 66 on correct Mutex-guarded code on both 6.3 and 6.4 (false positive), while the real race plant is only distinguishable by five differing plain-run counts; the promised gates/lint-carriers-and-sanitizers verdict was not on disk when written.

'unable to type-check this expression in reasonable time' can hide a real type error: Double+Float took 4128 ms to fail with that message and 74 ms with the true 'binary operator + cannot be applied' once split.
The SW-GATE-10 justification pass is unusable as a whole-tree gate on an adopted tree (2 legacy lines before and after migration); only the added-lines delta check goes red on the lazy migration.

SW-CORE-02 — Run every new check on a planted violation and on its compliant twin, outside the repo under test, and quote both results before relying on it.
SW-CORE-03 — Pass the find-based canary before trusting any empty grep, find or awk result, and never chain a failed canary with && before a semicolon.
SW-CORE-04 — Read the floor (SW-PKG-06) and record a baseline before the first edit, then prove the manifest in effect with a dump-package count after any manifest-editing tool.

SW-CORE-07 — Build swift-upgrade and swift-diagnose to the skill shape: body at most 500 lines, description at most 1024 characters opening with Use when and naming exact symptoms, depth in references/, checker exit 0.
SW-CORE-08 — Keep the swift-quality index under 200 lines with a routing row for every ID family, a sibling map, a bare **/*.swift glob and never-matching globs on depth files.
SW-CORE-09 — Pin the toolchain once in .swift-version and derive the primary CI image from it; literal tags only on deliberate matrix legs.
SW-CORE-10 — Add no hatch in an upgrade: resolve diagnostics by the SW-CONC-28 ladder and judge the result by the added-lines delta against the baseline commit.

SW-CORE-11 — Upgrade in order: baseline, floor and typo guard, flag probes (never committed), manifest enablement of non-zero-delta names, ladder, flip, clear warnings, -warnings-as-errors exit 0 on current and floor toolchains.
SW-CORE-12 — Adopt post-6 features with swift package migrate --target for the five migratable names, once each from a clean green tree, then re-gate on both toolchains.
SW-CORE-13 — Fold migrate's per-target enableUpcomingFeature literals into the shared package.targets loop and verify with fold-check.sh.
SW-CORE-14 — Run the four dated probes (SE-0526, SE-0540, SE-0529, T-V42) at every toolchain or SwiftPM bump; a compiling probe means the cited rules are stale.
SW-CORE-15 — Stop and report at stop conditions S1 to S6 instead of adding a hatch or an #if compiler split.
SW-CORE-16 — Classify every failure by exit code plus the first message line, never the code alone; 137, 141 and 143 mean look outside the program.
SW-CORE-17 — Never make a symptom stop by changing the measurement (enable=no, longer timeout, sleep, try?, nonisolated(unsafe), removed gate); accept a fix only when the same measurement clears.
SW-CORE-18 — Capture a hang before killing it: backtracer on, set -m launch with SigIgn bits 0x6 clear, SIGQUIT before SIGKILL, signal the test runner not swift-test.

SW-CORE-19 — Triage rc 0 nondeterminism with a TSan build, read the report kind first (data race versus Swift access race) with five plain runs as fallback, and branch exit 124 by leak line, CPU, then dump frame.

SW-CORE-20 — On unable to type-check in reasonable time split the expression and read the first real error; gate cost with -warn-long-expression-type-checking=100 and -warnings-as-errors, never raise a limit.
SW-CORE-21 — Start with consent on live processes and end every diagnose or upgrade run with the five-block receipt naming every rule ID relied on.

network/registry-clients: URLSessionConfiguration.timeoutIntervalForResource is a no-op in FoundationNetworking on Linux (6.4 and 6.3). Tuist's swifterpm relies on it for its total-transfer bound.

network/registry-clients: AHC's execute(deadline:) stops at the response head: the deadline task is cancelled when the head arrives. A 3 s deadline did not stop a body trickling for 7.5 s, and the README's timeout examples read like total caps.

network/registry-clients: HTTPClient.shared decodes gzip (decompression .enabled(limit: .ratio(25))), so blob digests mismatch for Content-Encoding: gzip layers. URLSession decodes always. Vapor's Application.swift:137 comments on this deliberately.

network/registry-clients: Neither client can trust a private CA through the environment on Linux. SSL_CERT_FILE is ignored by both, and URLSessionCertificateAuthorityInfoFile is compiled only under #if os(Android). Only AHC's TLSConfiguration.additionalTrustRoots works.

network/registry-clients: A per-task delegate argument on data(for:delegate:) never receives the redirect callback on Linux, and httpAdditionalHeaders also leaks the Authorization header. Both leaks reproduce on a port-only change as well as a host change.

network/registry-clients: containerization now has validateRealm (RegistryClient+Token.swift:217-236) and a no-redirect token client. swift-container-plugin's AuthHandler sends credentials to any challenge realm with no origin check and no token cache. registry:2 2.8.3 returns 404, not 406, for an OCI manifest requested without a matching Accept header.
